reason: The text demonstrates multiple instances of leaders and people collaborating and working together. The shepherds at the well collectively work to roll away the stone and water the flocks (וְנֶאֶסְפוּ...וְגָלֲל֤וּ אֶת־ הָאֶ֙בֶן֙...וְהִשְׁק֖וּ). Jacob, as a leader figure, engages with the shepherds and joins them in their work. Most significantly, Jacob and Laban establish a working relationship where they cooperate for mutual benefit over fourteen years. Additionally, Rachel and Leah actively collaborate with Jacob in deciding their departure from Laban's household, demonstrating unified family leadership. These examples show vertical collaboration (Jacob with workers/Laban) and horizontal collaboration (among community members), establishing a pattern of coordinated labor and shared decision-making.
